content: These results connect dynamics within individual denoising runs to variability across repeated inference. Within-trajectory dynamics contain information about whether independent repetitions of the same inference process will concentrate on a common endpoint or produce competing endpoints. This provides a concrete route towards estimating properties of the endpoint distribution with fewer complete generations.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: Language-model inference is stochastic. Repeated inference on the same input can produce different outputs, making the distribution of possible outputs or endpoints an important source of information about predictive uncertainty. A direct way to characterize this uncertainty is to sample the model repeatedly and measure the resulting endpoint distribution. This approach is conceptually simple but computationally expensive: estimating whether an output is stable, identifying competing endpoints, or measuring their entropy requires multiple complete generations for every input.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: Masked diffusion language models expose an additional source of information during inference. Rather than constructing an output through a strictly left-to-right sequence of next-token decisions, they iteratively transform an unresolved output state into a completed sequence. The inference process therefore exposes a temporal trajectory of convergence toward the eventual output. Recent work has begun to characterize these trajectories through token commitment, temporal stability, remasking sensitivity, and other measures of uncertainty during denoising [ 5 , 12 , 14 ] . A separate line of work has examined uncertainty in diffusion language models using repeated generations and trajectory-derived signals [ 10 ] . Together, these developments raise a more specific cross-scale question: does the convergence observed within denoising trajectories systematically relate to the distribution of endpoints obtained when the same inference process is repeated?

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: This question distinguishes two scales of concentration. Within a denoising trajectory, we can measure how much of the eventual output has resolved as inference progresses. Across repeated trajectories, we can measure how strongly stochastic inference concentrates on the same final answer. These quantities are different objects: the first describes how the eventual output resolves over the course of a single denoising run, whereas the second describes an empirical distribution over repeated runs. Their relationship is plausible from the structure of diffusion inference, but its empirical strength, temporal evolution, and limits are not determined by that observation alone.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: Establishing this relationship matters for uncertainty estimation. Across-run uncertainty is directly observable only after repeating inference. If properties visible during denoising systematically track the endpoint distribution produced across repetitions, then information about that distribution is already present in the trajectory of inference itself. This does not imply that a single trajectory recovers the endpoint distribution. It establishes the prerequisite for asking whether uncertainty that currently requires repeated sampling can eventually be estimated from one or a small number of denoising trajectories.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: We study this relationship in four masked diffusion language models: Dream Base, Dream Instruct, LLaDA-8B Base, and LLaDA-8B Instruct, across subsets of ARC Challenge, MMLU, GSM8K, and BIG-Bench Hard Boolean Expressions. For each model–dataset–question combination, we collect K = 20 K=20 independent stochastic generations, yielding 32,000 complete denoising trajectories and 1,600 question-level observations.

authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: For each trajectory, we define S ⁡ ( t ) S(t) as the fraction of the eventual scored output that has stably resolved by normalized denoising time t t . We summarize the full trajectory by its area under this convergence curve, c within c_{\mathrm{within}} , which measures within-trajectory concentration toward the realized endpoint. Across repeated trajectories, we define c across c_{\mathrm{across}} as the empirical mass assigned to the modal final answer and use Shannon entropy H H to characterize uncertainty in the resulting endpoint distribution. Our primary analysis asks whether variation in c within c_{\mathrm{within}} is associated with endpoint entropy. Temporal analyses then ask when this relationship becomes visible during denoising.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: We obtain four main findings. First, within-run convergence is systematically associated with across-run endpoint uncertainty. Higher c within c_{\mathrm{within}} is associated with lower endpoint entropy across multiple robustness specifications . The association remains statistically significant when analysis is restricted to multi-token outputs, where convergence contains richer trajectory structure than the reveal timing of a single answer token. It also strengthens when positive-entropy observations receive greater weight, indicating that the large mass of unanimous endpoint distributions attenuates rather than generates the pooled association.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: Second, within- and across-run concentration exhibit a strongly asymmetric empirical geometry . High within-run concentration almost exclusively accompanies high across-run concentration, whereas high across-run concentration frequently occurs despite substantially slower within-run convergence. The two forms of concentration are therefore related but not interchangeable.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: Third, this relationship develops during inference . The fraction of the eventual output already resolved at intermediate denoising times is associated with endpoint entropy, and the magnitude of this association increases as denoising progresses. Complementary time-to-convergence measures produce the corresponding pattern: later convergence is associated with higher endpoint entropy. The relationship is not uniform across tasks, however; dataset-specific estimates are significant for ARC, BBH, and MMLU but not GSM8K.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: Fourth, denoising dynamics predict endpoint competition in independent held-out runs . Features from a single trajectory predict whether repeated inference produces competing endpoints substantially better than model and dataset identity alone (AUROC 0.854 versus 0.753). As more trajectories are observed, their final outputs become increasingly informative, but trajectory dynamics provide complementary information: adding temporal features to observed-output features improves AUROC at each evaluated multi-trajectory budget. Thus, information about the endpoint regime is already present within individual denoising runs before that regime is directly observed through repeated inference.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: Finally, convergence does not imply correctness . Strong within-run convergence and highly concentrated, even unanimous, endpoint distributions can occur around an incorrect answer. The quantities studied here therefore characterize uncertainty in the model’s stochastic endpoint distribution rather than correctness of the endpoint.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: Taken together, these results connect dynamics within individual denoising runs to the distribution of endpoints produced across repeated inference. Whereas prior work has used denoising trajectories as uncertainty signals or to improve decoding, we show that within-trajectory dynamics predict a distinct object: whether independent repetitions of the same inference process will concentrate on a common endpoint or produce competing endpoints. This links uncertainty visible within a single realization to variability across realizations, and provides a concrete route toward estimating properties of the endpoint distribution with fewer complete generations.

content: At inference time, the model evaluates unresolved positions using the current partially generated sequence as context. A decoding policy then determines which positions are committed or unmasked before the next denoising step. Because masked positions can condition on visible tokens on either side, textual position and resolution order need not coincide. The resulting sequence of intermediate states, 𝐱 T → 𝐱 T − 1 → ⋯ → 𝐱 0 \mathbf{x}_{T}\rightarrow\mathbf{x}_{T-1}\rightarrow\cdots\rightarrow\mathbf{x}_{0} , therefore exposes an explicit trajectory through which the final output emerges.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: The availability of intermediate states has motivated recent work treating denoising time as an object of analysis rather than merely an implementation detail. Lu [5] studies the temporal emergence of information in LLaDA-8B-Base using token commitment, linear probes, confidence and entropy dynamics, and mid-trajectory perturbations. The study finds structured temporal variation in the information available during denoising, including differences in when linguistic properties become recoverable and in uncertainty between tokens that eventually resolve correctly and incorrectly.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: Temporal information can also be useful directly for decoding. Wu and Huang [12] argues that token-selection rules based only on confidence at a single denoising step discard information contained in the preceding trajectory. Their Stability-Weighted Decoding method measures temporal instability through changes in predictive distributions across consecutive steps and uses this history to modify token commitment decisions, improving generation performance on mathematical reasoning and code-generation tasks.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: A related question concerns where commitment occurs. Yeom et al. [14] shows that commitment order in diffusion language models can depart substantially from textual order on reasoning tasks. In unrestricted LLaDA decoding on GSM8K, answer-bearing positions can commit while much of the preceding reasoning text remains unresolved. Restricting long-range commitment changes both generation behavior and reasoning accuracy. These results show that denoising trajectories contain structure not captured simply by the final output or by the number of completed denoising steps.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: Together, this literature establishes that commitment time, commitment order, and temporal stability are informative properties of diffusion inference. The present work builds on this trajectory-level view but studies a different quantity: the cumulative fraction of the eventual output that has stably resolved as inference progresses.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: Uncertainty in language generation is commonly estimated from either model probabilities or repeated stochastic generations. Sampling-based approaches characterize the distribution over completed outputs directly and underpin methods such as self-consistency [ 11 , 4 ] . For structured prediction, dispersion across complete sequences provides information that is not available from an isolated token probability [ 6 ] . The cost is that estimating such distributions requires multiple complete inference runs.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: This trade-off is particularly relevant for diffusion language models, whose iterative trajectories provide additional candidate uncertainty signals. Vazhentsev et al. [10] presents a systematic study of uncertainty quantification for large language diffusion models and derives trajectory-based signals from intermediate generations, remasking dynamics, and denoising complexity. Their methods approach stronger sampling-based uncertainty baselines at substantially lower computational cost, demonstrating that the denoising process itself contains information relevant to uncertainty estimation.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: The trajectory-based quantities considered in this literature primarily use intermediate dynamics to predict properties such as correctness or hallucination, or to improve the decoding procedure itself. Repeated sampling, by contrast, directly reveals how probability mass is distributed across the endpoints produced by stochastic inference. These constitute different observational scales of the same generative process.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
section: Local and Global Signals in Language-Model Inference.
content: A related line of work considers whether measurements defined at different scales of an inference process provide consistent information about model behavior. In sequential LLM decision systems, local perturbations to input information can propagate into global instability across a sequence of decisions, showing that locally plausible outputs need not compose into stable sequential behavior [ 1 ] . More directly, Amador Diaz Lopez [2] distinguishes local confidence, measured from the probability of a selected answer token, from global confidence, measured from modal-answer frequency under repeated stochastic inference. The two signals are not empirically interchangeable, and their disagreement is associated with sampling instability.

content: These findings motivate a broader cross-scale question: what can information observed within an individual inference process reveal about behavior that emerges across repeated realizations of that process? Masked diffusion language models provide a particularly rich setting for this question because a single generation exposes an entire denoising trajectory rather than only a token-level confidence signal. This motivates the within–across distinction considered here.

At each normalized inference time t t , some fraction of the eventual output may already have stably resolved. Tracking this fraction produces a convergence trajectory S ⁡ ( t ) S(t) describing how the realized endpoint emerges within an inference run.

authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: Existing commitment-time analyses ask when particular positions or fractions of an output become stable, while trajectory-based uncertainty methods use intermediate states as diagnostic signals. The question considered here is instead explicitly cross-scale, i.e., whether within-trajectory convergence dynamics are related to across-trajectory endpoint uncertainty .

content: There is no requirement that the two measurements coincide. A set of trajectories may converge relatively slowly within individual runs yet repeatedly terminate at the same endpoint, while stochastic competition among endpoints may be accompanied by different within-run dynamics. The empirical questions are therefore whether these two scales co-vary, when during denoising such a relationship becomes visible, and what information within-run convergence provides about the endpoint distribution observed under repeated inference.

Complementary time-to-convergence measures show the corresponding pattern: later convergence is associated with higher endpoint entropy, with β ^ = 0.223 \hat{\beta}=0.223 for T 50 T_{50} , 0.106 0.106 for T 90 T_{90} , 0.094 0.094 for T 95 T_{95} , and 0.092 0.092 for T 100 T_{100} (See Table 3 in Appendix A ).

The uncontrolled association is positive ( β ^ = 0.186 \hat{\beta}=0.186 , p = 0.010 p=0.010 ), but is not robust to model and dataset fixed effects: with both fixed effects, the estimate is negative but imprecise ( β ^ = − 0.326 \hat{\beta}=-0.326 , p = 0.221 p=0.221 ). authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: The principal negative association is robust to alternative standard-error estimators, clustering by benchmark item, restrictions to multi- and single-token outputs, separate base and instruction-tuned models, separate Dream and LLaDA-8B families, and exclusion of near-degenerate c within c_{\mathrm{within}} cells. The multi-token-only estimate remains statistically significant ( β ^ = − 0.089 \hat{\beta}=-0.089 , p = 0.036 p=0.036 ), although smaller than the full-sample estimate; GSM8K is the principal task-level exception.

authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: Because 84.0% of observations have H = 0 H=0 , we additionally test whether this mass mechanically generates the pooled association using 10,000 balanced bootstrap replicates within model–dataset cells. Under the 50% positive-entropy target, the achieved share is 43.75% because Dream Base/BBH-bool and Dream Instruct/ARC contain no positive-entropy observations. The mean bootstrap coefficient is − 0.4517 -0.4517 (median − 0.4517 -0.4517 , SD = 0.0136 =0.0136 ), with percentile 95% bootstrap interval [ − 0.4783 , − 0.4254 ] [-0.4783,-0.4254] ; all 10,000 coefficient estimates are negative.

authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: The result strengthens as positive-entropy observations receive greater weight (See Table 4 and Figure 2 in Appendix A ): mean coefficients are − 0.4094 -0.4094 , − 0.4517 -0.4517 , and − 0.4835 -0.4835 under 40%, 50%, and 60% positive-entropy targets, respectively. Thus, the negative pooled association is not an artifact of the 84% zero-entropy mass; under these deliberately reweighted designs, greater weight on positive-entropy observations moves the coefficient further from zero. These bootstrap intervals describe resampling variability under fixed balancing and are not population confidence intervals.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
section: A Single Denoising Trajectory Predicts Endpoint Competition.
content: We next test whether denoising dynamics from a small number of trajectories predict whether independent held-out runs produce competing endpoints. Using a single trajectory, temporal features predict endpoint competition with an AUROC of 0.854 (95% interval [0.850, 0.857]), compared with 0.753 [0.750, 0.758] using model and dataset identity alone. Macro-F1 similarly increases from 0.407 [0.402, 0.410] to 0.513 [0.499, 0.525]. Because a single observed final output contains no information about across-run multiplicity by construction, this result shows that the denoising trajectory contains predictive information about the outcomes of independent repeated inference.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
section: A Single Denoising Trajectory Predicts Endpoint Competition.
content: The predictive value of trajectory dynamics remains approximately stable as the number of observed trajectories increases, with temporal-feature AUROC between 0.851 and 0.854 for k ∈ { 1 , 2 , 3 , 5 } k\in\{1,2,3,5\} . In contrast, prediction from the observed final outputs improves with repeated sampling, reaching AUROC 0.891 at k = 5 k=5 . The two sources of information are complementary: adding temporal features to observed-output features improves AUROC by 0.070, 0.057, and 0.040 at k = 2 k=2 , 3 3 , and 5 5 , respectively, with all 95% intervals excluding zero. Thus, within-trajectory dynamics provide information about subsequent endpoint competition beyond that available from a small sample of final outputs (See Figure 1 in Appendix A ).

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
section: Endpoint Concentration Does Not Imply Correctness.
content: Both concentration measures are positively associated with correctness. In separate model- and dataset-controlled logistic regressions, a 0.1 increase in c within c_{\mathrm{within}} corresponds to an odds ratio of 1.187 (95% CI [1.134, 1.243], p = 1.6 × 10 − 13 p=1.6\times 10^{-13} ), while the corresponding odds ratio for c across c_{\mathrm{across}} is 1.389 (95% CI [1.235, 1.562], p = 3.9 × 10 − 8 p=3.9\times 10^{-8} ). When both are included jointly, each remains statistically significant, with odds ratios of 1.157 for c within c_{\mathrm{within}} and 1.272 for c across c_{\mathrm{across}} .

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
section: Endpoint Concentration Does Not Imply Correctness.
content: Strong concentration nevertheless does not imply correctness. At τ = 0.9 \tau=0.9 , 78 questions exhibit both high within-run and high across-run concentration while having an incorrect modal answer, comprising 4.9% of the full sample and 13.4% of all incorrect observations. Among these stable-wrong cases, 98.7% are unanimous across all 20 runs, and 12 benchmark items exhibit the same failure in at least two primary models.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: The results connect two observational scales of diffusion inference. Within a single denoising run, the eventual output progressively resolves from an initially uncertain state. Across repeated runs, stochastic inference produces a distribution over final endpoints. These are distinct objects, but the experiments show that they are systematically related: stronger convergence within individual runs is associated with greater concentration across runs, and information about this across-run regime becomes increasingly visible as denoising proceeds.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
section: Within-run convergence characterizes the endpoint regime.
content: The joint distribution reveals a strongly asymmetric relationship. High c within c_{\mathrm{within}} almost exclusively accompanies high c across c_{\mathrm{across}} , whereas high c across c_{\mathrm{across}} frequently occurs alongside lower within-run concentration. Repeated trajectories can therefore concentrate on the same endpoint even when within-run concentration is relatively low, but high within-run concentration is rarely observed when repeated inference produces a dispersed endpoint distribution.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
section: Within-run convergence characterizes the endpoint regime.
content: The entropy analysis provides a continuous counterpart to this geometry. Higher c within c_{\mathrm{within}} is associated with lower endpoint entropy, and the association persists across the principal robustness analyses. Importantly, reweighting the sample toward positive-entropy observations strengthens rather than weakens the relationship. The large mass of unanimous endpoint distributions therefore attenuates, rather than generates, the pooled association.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: The connection between these two scales is already visible before inference terminates. Greater resolved mass at intermediate denoising times is associated with lower endpoint entropy, and the magnitude of this association increases as denoising progresses. Complementary time-to-convergence measures show the corresponding pattern: later convergence accompanies greater endpoint uncertainty.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: This temporal structure matters because the final endpoint alone does not contain the path by which it was reached. Two runs may terminate at the same answer while differing substantially in when and how strongly that answer resolved during denoising. The results show that this intermediate trajectory contains information about a property that is defined only across repeated runs: the concentration of the resulting endpoint distribution.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: The held-out prediction experiment makes this connection explicit. Features from a single denoising trajectory predict whether independent repetitions of the same inference process will produce a common endpoint or competing endpoints, substantially improving over model and dataset identity alone. As additional runs become available, their observed final outputs become increasingly informative, but trajectory dynamics remain complementary: combining temporal and observed-output features improves prediction beyond the observed outputs alone.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: This result places the present findings in a broader trajectory-based uncertainty literature. Prior work has shown that intermediate denoising states can provide useful uncertainty signals or improve decoding. The quantity predicted here is different: it is a property of the distribution generated across independent realizations of inference. The denoising path within one realization therefore contains information about variability across realizations.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: This distinction also gives the result a direct practical interpretation. Repeated sampling remains necessary to observe the empirical endpoint distribution itself, but some information obtained from those repetitions is already available within individual denoising runs. Trajectory dynamics may therefore complement repeated sampling when estimating whether inference is concentrated or competitive, potentially reducing the number of complete generations required to characterize stochastic model behavior.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: Concentration should nevertheless not be conflated with correctness. Highly concentrated and even unanimous endpoint distributions can converge on an incorrect answer. The quantities studied here characterize uncertainty in the model’s stochastic endpoint distribution rather than calibration to ground truth.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: The primary analysis covers four irreversible masked-diffusion models from two model families. LLaDA2.1-mini, for example, is excluded because resolved positions can subsequently be edited, changing the interpretation of stable resolution; whether the same within–across relationship extends to editable or continuous diffusion models remains open. The relationship is also task-dependent, with GSM8K providing the principal exception to the cross-task pattern.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: Output geometry affects c within c_{\mathrm{within}} . For single-token irreversible outputs, it is algebraically determined by answer-token reveal time. Although the association remains significant for multi-token outputs, its magnitude is substantially smaller. The strength of the observed relationship should therefore not be assumed invariant to output structure or denoising schedule.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: Across-run quantities are estimated from K = 20 K=20 trajectories and remain finite-sample approximations to the underlying endpoint distribution. The competing-endpoint subset is also substantially smaller than the full sample, limiting precision when characterizing dispersion conditional on competition. Finally, the association analyses are observational: they establish systematic covariation between within-run convergence and across-run endpoint uncertainty, not that faster convergence causes lower endpoint uncertainty.

title: From Denoising Dynamics to Endpoint Uncertainty in Diffusion Language Models
authors: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez
content: Taken together, the results show that the trajectory of a single denoising run and the distribution produced across repeated runs are linked at two different scales of the same stochastic inference process. Within-run dynamics do more than correlate with endpoint uncertainty: they predict whether independent repetitions will concentrate on a common endpoint or produce competing endpoints. This cross-scale relationship provides a basis for uncertainty methods that use information exposed during denoising to characterize across-run variability with fewer complete generations.

section: NeSySpec: Neuro-Symbolic Technical Intelligence for Auditing Engineering Specifications with an Application to Aircraft
content: Engineers who audit a declared specification of an engineered system need to know which physical constraints it respects, which it violates, which field was altered and how to correct it. NeSySpec is an integrated and interpretable neuro-symbolic audit framework, built on Logic Tensor Networks, that answers these questions in one pipeline. Its axioms encode the physical relations of the domain as differentiable graded predicates whose tolerances are learned from a fleet of real records; from the same degrees, it diagnoses the violated constraint, identifies the altered field by abduction, proposes a minimum-change correction and ties image evidence to the parts it describes, abstaining exactly where evidence is missing, and returns all of it in one verification report. We validate NeSySpec on 107 aircraft types, with 16 test aircraft of 9 families held out of training, on specification records paired with ground photographs and satellite imagery and on synthetic errors: generated corruptions, edits labeled from the edit alone and deliberate falsifications. NeSySpec combines all the assessed audit outputs in one pipeline, which no learned, rule-based, solver-based, neuro-symbolic or language-model comparator does; on the test aircraft none is ahead of it in the macro-F1 of its constraint verdicts, in naming the violated constraint and the altered field or in the repair error, and it is competitive in record and image-pair detection. Its diagnosis names the violated constraint in 94.2% of corrupted test records, against 79.5% for classical Fellegi-Holt diagnosis, and on edits labeled from the edit alone, without retraining, abduction finds the altered field in 59.3% of records, against 30.6% for minimum-cardinality localization with random tie-breaking. Only the knowledge base, the visual predicates, the corruption generator and the data are specific to the domain.

content: Certification, maintenance and procurement engineers work with engineered systems they did not design and reverse-engineer them from declared specifications of masses, dimensions, ratings and performance. A record can be incomplete, inconsistent, valid for another variant or misreported, and public knowledge bases hold wrong numerical values [ 1 ] ; the errors of a record propagate into the performance models it feeds [ 2 ] . Auditing such records falls within the scope of civil technical intelligence, which gathers and assesses information about technologies and technical products [ 3 , 4 ] . Technical intelligence increasingly draws on open sources [ 5 , 6 ] . For aircraft, photographs and satellite imagery can also help verify the visually observable attributes reported in the specifications [ 7 , 8 ] . We use reverse engineering in a first-approach sense: inferring which physical relations a declared specification and, when available, its image respect or violate, which field departs from them and which value restores them. authors: Pier Mattia Basciano, Gianvito Antenori, Cristiano Andolfi, Giovanni Farina, Salvatore Monteleone
content: Learned methods, from anomaly detectors to tabular foundation models and language models, score each record [ 9 , 10 , 11 ] , with field-level attributions [ 12 ] . Statistical data editing and consistency-based diagnosis identify violated constraints and the fields implicated in those violations, based on bounds set by experts [ 13 , 14 ] . Neuro-Symbolic Artificial Intelligence (NeSy) integrates learning with explicit knowledge and reasoning [ 15 , 16 ] , also surveyed for advanced air mobility [ 17 ] , and can learn such bounds from data together with the constraints they delimit. To our knowledge, no previous work provides and evaluates together the outputs that such an audit needs, from the violated constraint and the altered field to part-grounded image evidence and a report (Table 2 ).

title: NeSySpec: Neuro-Symbolic Technical Intelligence for Auditing Engineering Specifications with an Application to Aircraft
authors: Pier Mattia Basciano, Gianvito Antenori, Cristiano Andolfi, Giovanni Farina, Salvatore Monteleone
content: We present NeSySpec, an integrated and interpretable neuro-symbolic framework for auditing engineering specifications, built on Logic Tensor Networks (LTN) [ 19 ] : trained on fleet data, it determines through its logical axioms which physical constraints a declared record respects and which it violates, and returns a verification report (Figures 1 and 5 ). Its graded predicates measure each physical, definitional or regulatory relation by its residual against bands learned from the training fleet, and cross-modal axioms compare the fields with what a vision module reads. Masked quantification gives NeSySpec exact abstention on missing evidence: each verdict reduces to the constraints that the available evidence makes checkable, and the report lists every undeclared field with the constraints it leaves unchecked. The audit proceeds from detection to diagnosis and repair. It first scores the record using a masked mean of constraint violation degrees. This overall verdict can then be traced back to individual constraints, with the largest violation degree identifying the most violated constraint. An abductive search over single-field changes then localizes the altered field. Finally, a minimum-change repair searches for the smallest adjustment that restores coherence. A grounding axiom encourages each visual head to place its class-activation evidence on the part its predicate describes, so that the report ties image evidence to parts.

title: NeSySpec: Neuro-Symbolic Technical Intelligence for Auditing Engineering Specifications with an Application to Aircraft
authors: Pier Mattia Basciano, Gianvito Antenori, Cristiano Andolfi, Giovanni Farina, Salvatore Monteleone
content: We validate NeSySpec on 107 aircraft, with specification records, FGVC-Aircraft photographs [ 7 ] and RarePlanes satellite imagery [ 8 ] , holding 16 test aircraft of 9 families out of training, and evaluate constraint verdicts and diagnosis, field localization and repair, record coherence, missing evidence and absent images, the grounding of the visual axioms and robustness to deliberate falsification, on errors labeled by the corruption generator and on errors labeled from the edit alone (Section 4 ). The constraint verdicts reach a macro-F1 of 0.795 on generator labels and, without retraining, 0.575 on intervention labels, above a network trained with the DL2 loss on the same residuals and targets, the like-for-like neuro-symbolic test, and find every labeled violation in 0.934 of generator-labeled test corruptions against 0.522 for that network, with micro precision on par on test and lower on the unseen class (Section 4.2 , Appendix ). The largest-violation key identifies the violated constraint in 0.942 of generator-labeled test corruptions, outperforming Fellegi–Holt, solver-based and rule-based diagnosis, DL2 applied to the declared fields, and a prompted language model. Abduction then traces the error to an individual field, correctly identifying the altered field in 0.593 of independently labeled errors. By comparison, minimum-cardinality localization reaches 0.306 with random tie-breaking and 0.453 with oracle tie-breaking; a sizing-regression residual also reaches 0.453 (Figure 6 ). The record verdict detects incoherent records at a test AUROC of 0.979 on generator labels, and on satellite pairs the multimodal verifier, which names the contradicted axiom, detects incoherent record-image pairs at 0.994 over all pair types, against 0.748 for a prompted vision-language model (Section 4.4 ). Table 5 lines these results up. No comparator returns every output of the audit, and on the test aircraft no comparator is ahead of NeSySpec in the macro-F1 of the constraint verdicts, in naming the violated constraint and the altered field or in the repair error on the altered field; in record and pair detection, learners on the residuals and late fusions are close to it and in some settings rank higher (Section 4.1 ).

title: NeSySpec: Neuro-Symbolic Technical Intelligence for Auditing Engineering Specifications with an Application to Aircraft
authors: Pier Mattia Basciano, Gianvito Antenori, Cristiano Andolfi, Giovanni Farina, Salvatore Monteleone
content: Among the approaches evaluated here - the DL2 method on the declared fields, the network trained with the DL2 loss on the same residuals read per constraint, a constraint-layer repair ordering, LTN ablations, solver and rule diagnosis and prompted language and vision-language models -, NeSySpec is, to our knowledge, the most suitable neuro-symbolic framework for auditing engineering specifications: it provides and evaluates together the seven outputs of Table 2 , from constraint verdicts and field localization to part-grounded image evidence and a verification report. Its logic contributes more to the physical audit than to record classification. Training its knowledge base through Real Logic (the differentiable formulation of first-order fuzzy logic underlying LTN [ 19 ] ) improves detection over the same knowledge base left at its initial values. Detection also improves as more knowledge is encoded, a trend shared by a residual MLP using the same constraints (Section 4.8 ). Only the knowledge base, visual predicates, corruption generator and data of NeSySpec are aircraft-specific, so another engineered system enters through these four parts (Appendix A ).

content: Our formulation of the audit in Real Logic has four properties. First, the bands and slopes of graded predicates are learned through their truth values, jointly with the record verdict. Second, guarded quantification uses evidence availability as its guard: constraints whose required evidence is missing are excluded, and the verdict reduces exactly to that of the available constraints (Proposition 1 ). Third, physical predicates and visual heads share a common truth scale, allowing cross-modal axioms to enter the same knowledge base. Finally, the grounding axiom uses the Reichenbach implication to scale the localization pressure with the truth of the visual predicate.

Each axiom therefore retains its own truth value at inference, and the record verdict decomposes into constraint-level verdicts. Crisp rule validation also provides exact abstention (Table 2 ), and Section 4.8 examines the contribution of each of the four properties.

section: Reverse engineering, specification records and data editing.
content: Physics-driven correction flags machine-learning estimates of design parameters, such as those of an aero engine, whose accumulated physical error exceeds a threshold, and corrects them by surrogate-assisted optimization against physical evaluations [ 22 ] ; NeSySpec works from fleet data without a simulator and names the constraint that fails. Fellegi–Holt editing localizes errors by finding the minimum-weight set of fields whose modification satisfies every edit [ 13 ] . Data validation leaves a rule with a missing value unevaluated [ 23 ] . Data repair methods, benchmarked by Ni et al. [ 24 ] , correct cells through probabilistic inference under integrity constraints in HoloClean [ 25 ] or using a few example repairs in Baran [ 26 ] . The satisfiability modulo theories (SMT) solver Z3 [ 27 ] returns conflict sets for consistency-based diagnosis [ 14 ] as unsatisfiable cores. It also supports minimum-cardinality localization through MaxSMT [ 28 ] . Rule engines and language models check building designs against codes [ 29 , 30 ] . Their bounds, where present, are crisp, set by experts or mined from data [ 31 ] , and they take no image evidence; NeSySpec grades every constraint against bands learned from the fleet, ranks the violated constraints by the graded degrees of its own verdict, localizes the altered field by abduction with no oracle to break ties and adds image evidence (Sections 4.2 and 4.3 ). A reference architecture for auditing mechanical engineering drawings checks the entities read from them against a standards knowledge graph [ 32 ] . Hybrid fault diagnosis pairs model-based residuals with anomaly classifiers [ 33 ] , or residuals learned from fault-free data with consistency-based isolation [ 34 ] , and a neuro-symbolic architecture lets knowledge-based and learned methods support each other in anomaly detection and fault diagnosis [ 35 ] , a division of labor that NeSySpec offers as its optional rank-then-explain alarm, a residual-learner alarm explained by the violated constraint.

content: TabPFN v2 [ 10 ] and AnoLLM [ 11 ] score records by in-context learning and language-model likelihood, RegValidator checks the detection ideas of a language model with data-validation rules [ 36 ] , GIDCL detects and corrects errors with a graph network and cleaning rules generated by a language model [ 37 ] , and ZeroED detects erroneous values without manual labels through language-model reasoning [ 38 ] . NeSySpec returns, for each record, which constraints the record respects and which it violates, the altered field, a repair proposal and the evidence coverage, together with a score; Section 4.4 compares the scores in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve - AUROC.

title: NeSySpec: Neuro-Symbolic Technical Intelligence for Auditing Engineering Specifications with an Application to Aircraft
authors: Pier Mattia Basciano, Gianvito Antenori, Cristiano Andolfi, Giovanni Farina, Salvatore Monteleone
content: Neuro-symbolic methods use explicit knowledge to guide learning and reasoning. Frameworks such as LTN, DeepProbLog [ 42 ] , Scallop [ 43 ] and NeurASP [ 44 ] combine trainable models with logical reasoning. Knowledge can also enter through training objectives or mechanisms that constrain or refine predictions, as in abductive learning [ 45 ] , DL2 [ 20 ] , the semantic loss [ 46 ] , constraint layers [ 47 , 64 ] and Knowledge Enhanced Neural Networks (KENN) [ 48 ] . Probabilistic soft logic (PSL) infers truth values for open atoms under weighted rules [ 50 ] . Logic Explained Networks (LEN) extract rules from a trained network [ 49 ] . These frameworks can compute a truth, a probability or a distance to satisfaction per formula, from which a violated constraint can be read by an argmax or argmin, can carry a tolerance band as a neural or weighted predicate, and marginalize, infer or leave free what is unobserved (Table 2 , note b). Encoding NeSySpec’s knowledge base in DeepProbLog, Scallop or PSL would change its axiomatic and logical structure, with probabilistic facts and proofs in place of graded truths and masked quantification, so that comparison is left to future work (Section 5 ). NeSySpec joins these per-constraint truths with tolerance bands learned from the fleet, abstention under missing evidence (Proposition 1 ), a search for the altered field with its repair through the same degrees, part-grounded image evidence and a per-record report, provided and evaluated together, which no cited work does; Sections 4.2 and 4.8 compare it with the DL2 method on the declared fields and with a network trained with the DL2 loss on the same residuals, which returns per-constraint probabilities. LTN has grounded part-of relations, fault signatures, process traces [ 39 , 65 , 66 ] , fault-diagnosis rules for gearboxes and rotating machinery [ 40 , 41 ] and medical rules with learnable thresholds [ 18 ] ; an answer set program names the missing, misplaced or wrongly connected component of electrical control panels after a separately trained detector [ 55 ] , and GuardEn executes compiled safety rules on scene graphs of an image [ 56 ] ; NeSySpec adds graded constraints against bands learned from the fleet and visual predicates grounded in the parts they describe (Section 4.6 ).

title: NeSySpec: Neuro-Symbolic Technical Intelligence for Auditing Engineering Specifications with an Application to Aircraft

content: Explanation-guided learning adds supervision on model explanations [ 67 ] . Right for the Right Reasons (RRR) penalizes input gradients in regions annotated as irrelevant [ 57 ] , while GradMask penalizes them outside the annotated region [ 58 ] . RES learns from imprecise human masks [ 59 ] . The Energy loss of Rao et al. [ 60 ] increases the share of positive attribution inside annotated bounding boxes, and Pukdee et al. [ 61 ] learn from explanation constraints satisfied in expectation. NeSySpec expresses part-level supervision as an axiom on each head’s class-activation map, gated by the head’s assertion and guarded by part visibility. Section 4.6 compares this approach with RRR, GradMask and Pukdee et al. under a common protocol.

content: TIP pre-trains on images and masked tables for incomplete tabular data [ 62 ] , and AutoGluon-Multimodal (AutoGluon-MM) fuses tables and images with foundation models [ 63 ] . The fused verdict of NeSySpec aggregates its strata without labels and reduces exactly to the available constraints, and Section 4.4 compares it with these fusions; its cross-modal axioms read the attributes predicted by the visual heads, as concept bottleneck models predict a label from predicted concepts [ 68 ] . Open vision-language models [ 53 , 69 ] can judge whether a record and an image agree and a language model [ 52 ] whether a record is coherent, and vision-language models have been benchmarked on engineering rules, computer-aided design renderings and drawings, where they still struggle [ 54 ] ; NeSySpec returns with its judgment a verdict for every constraint (Section 4.4 ).

title: NeSySpec: Neuro-Symbolic Technical Intelligence for Auditing Engineering Specifications with an Application to Aircraft
authors: Pier Mattia Basciano, Gianvito Antenori, Cristiano Andolfi, Giovanni Farina, Salvatore Monteleone
content: Table 2 compares the reviewed approaches on seven outputs needed for specification auditing: identification of the violated constraint, localization of the altered field, a repair proposal, exact abstention under missing evidence, learned tolerances, part-grounded image evidence, and a per-record verification report. To our knowledge, none of the reviewed works provides and evaluates all seven outputs together. Statistical data editing and validation come closest, with crisp bounds set by experts or fitted to data and no image evidence. The neuro-symbolic formulation of NeSySpec uses graded constraint violation degrees for the largest-violation key and for abductive field localization, without an oracle to break ties (Sections 4.2 and 4.3 ).

title: NeSySpec: Neuro-Symbolic Technical Intelligence for Auditing Engineering Specifications with an Application to Aircraft
authors: Pier Mattia Basciano, Gianvito Antenori, Cristiano Andolfi, Giovanni Farina, Salvatore Monteleone
content: NeSySpec audits a declared record in one integrated, interpretable NeSy framework: through its logical axioms it gives a held or violated verdict on each physical relation that binds the record’s fields and, when an image is paired with it, on whether the image agrees. The framework is organized into seven modules (Figure 1 ), built on Real Logic (Section 2.1 ). Guarded quantification allows each axiom to contribute only when its required evidence is available (E1), while graded predicates express how well each constraint is satisfied (E2). A grounding axiom ties visual predictions to the relevant image parts (E3), and stratification preserves a separate verdict for each evidence source (E4). A monotone second head complements the main verdict with an additional score and diagnosis key (E5).

content: The specification benchmark splits the records by family: the business-jet families form the unseen class, six random families the unseen families, and the others fill training, validation and test at 60/20/20 (Appendix ). Each clean record yields up to two instances of each of five corruption families: an impossible single value and geometric, performance and cruise inconsistencies multiply or divide one field by 1 + ϵ 1+\epsilon , with ϵ = 0.05 \epsilon=0.05 and 0.10 0.10 , and a cross-class block swap (Frankenstein) copies a coherent block of fields from another class in the same split. The generator oracle, a crisp check of the same relations against class bands [ 0.88 ​ min , 1.12 ​ max ] [0.88\min,\,1.12\max] of each quantity over all 107 clean aircraft of every split, keeps an instance only when it flags the target constraint (any constraint for a swap); otherwise ϵ \epsilon doubles, for at most six attempts (Table ; realized instances in Figure 2 (d)). The verifier is fitted on training-split instances only: the oracle’s bands reach it through their labels and per-constraint targets, which thus carry the class extremes of all 107 aircraft, and no field value of another split enters training. Two noisy-but-coherent controls per record perturb each continuous field by a Gaussian factor with relative standard deviation 0.02, with 𝐴𝑅 \mathit{AR} rescaled according to the induced change in b 2 / S b^{2}/S ; both controls must remain coherent. The intervention benchmark (2,582 rows, same aircraft and splits) draws the same operators once per magnitude, without escalation or oracle certification, and labels each row from the edit alone. A row is labeled incoherent when a continuous field differs from its clean source by more than three noise standard deviations or an integer field changes. These tolerances are fixed before generation, and the label applies regardless of whether a physical relation is violated. An available constraint receives a positive label when its scope includes such an altered field. Noisy copies and edits within tolerance count as unaltered. These labels evaluate the constraint verdicts, the diagnosis key, abduction and detection. The satellite and multimodal benchmarks likewise include corrupted examples and controls. In the multimodal benchmark, each image is paired with its matching record, a mismatched record, or an altered version of its matching record. Mismatches involve aircraft from another class or role, or a sister variant. Occluded and degraded photographs serve as controls..

content: The train prior fits every data-dependent band on the 44 clean training aircraft and widens it to [ 0.88 ​ min , 1.12 ​ max ] [0.88\min,\,1.12\max] , as the oracle does. The bands start from the train prior and are learned with their slopes from the fleet and its labeled corruptions, so they act as learned tolerances: 45.7% of them keep both edges inside the training fleet range widened in the same way, and the others, all wing-loading bands among them, extend beyond it after training (Appendix ). The learned slopes act as implicit per-constraint weights. In hierarchical banks each band or tolerance parameter of a class is a fleet value plus a class offset with the same weight, so a class without training aircraft, such as the business jets, is read with fleet statistics and parameters. The remote-sensing axioms follow the same recipe: six graded slots (R1, R2 for civil and for military roles, R3, R4 and R10) read the residual in standard units of the clean training rows, and the logical axioms R5 to R9 enter as the negative logarithm of their truth. Each tabular stratum’s settings (the power p p of a masked power mean of the degrees, the in-band term, flat or hierarchical banks) are chosen on validation alone among eight candidates trained with eight seeds each; both strata select p = 1 p=1 , the masked mean of Eq. ( 9 ), and on generator-oracle labels the specification stratum keeps the in-band term and hierarchical banks.

content: NeSySpec’s audit has three optional settings. With rank-then-explain , the residual MLP, an MLP on the 14 physical quantities of the oracle (Table ), raises the alarm at its validation Youden threshold and the largest-violation key explains each flagged record; the flagged-and-diagnosed rate, the share of corrupted records flagged with a violated top-ranked constraint, scores this setting. The critical-field alert flags a record that leaves undeclared a field required by an applicable axiom and declared by at least 95% of the training records of its class - or of its engine type for classes with fewer than five training records -, reading only the undeclared fields, the class, the engine type and a table of the training records; with it enabled, NeSySpec flags a record when its verdict or the alert fires. With MICE imputation of the missing fields enabled, NeSySpec scores imputed values in place of abstaining on them; Section 4.5 compares this setting with learners given the same imputer.

content: Table 4 maps each benchmark to its labels and to the sections that use it; every error in this study is synthetic, an edit or a constructed mismatch of public records and images. Two label families recur. Generator labels come from the generator oracle of Section 3.1 , which judges the same residual quantities as the knowledge base against class bands fitted on all 107 aircraft; its single-field corruptions are escalated from 5 or 10% until the oracle flags them, mostly to 20 to 160% (geometric ones stay at 5 or 10%; Table ). Intervention labels cover single-field edits drawn once at 5 to 80% and cross-class block swaps: a field counts as altered beyond three noise standard deviations (0.06 in natural-log units for continuous fields, 0.134 for the aspect ratio, any change of an integer field), so edits within this tolerance, e.g., the 5% edits of continuous fields, count as unaltered, and a constraint is labeled when its scope contains an altered field. Such a constraint is involved in the edit, which need not violate it: an edit can keep the record inside the physical envelope of the fleet, and 613 of the 1,810 altered rows, about a third, break no constraint even under bands fitted on all 107 aircraft, so that no physical check can flag them (Appendix ). Generator labels follow the same relations as the axioms and were NeSySpec’s per-constraint training targets; intervention labels, set from the edit alone, are independent of them. Minimum-cardinality localization (Fellegi-Holt and MaxSMT [ 28 ] , all optimal solutions) breaks ties at random unless the oracle tie-break is named.

We call V V the record verdict and the held or violated outputs per constraint the constraint verdicts. The constraint verdicts use exact-set agreement per record, macro-F1 over the constraints with at least five labeled violations and the false-violation rate on clean records. Diagnosis and localization use top-1 rates, repair the log-space error and grounding the pointing game [ 89 ] ; detection scores the record verdict by AUROC and the false-positive rate (FPR) on the 32 controls at a true-positive rate (TPR) of 0.90. Experiments ran on an AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D with 192 GB of RAM, an NVIDIA RTX 5090 and an RTX 4090. Per record, the verdict and the key take one pass through the knowledge base, abduction evaluates the verdict at 1,201 log-space steps for each field read by an available constraint, and the repair solves one augmented-Lagrangian problem; training curves are in Appendix .

content: Table 5 lines up NeSySpec with its comparators on every output of the audit. Learners on the physical residuals return a record score and need a second model, a head per constraint or attributions, for a verdict or a diagnosis; solvers return a violated set, an edit or a repair; language and vision-language models return a judgment. NeSySpec is the only method that returns every output, and without an image its fused verdict alone returns the record verdict exactly. On the test aircraft no comparator is ahead of it in the macro-F1 of the constraint verdicts, in naming the violated constraint and the altered field or in the repair error on the altered field; the network trained with the DL2 loss keeps fewer false violations (Section 4.2 ). In record and pair detection, learners on the residuals and late fusions are close to NeSySpec and in some settings rank records or pairs higher (Sections 4.4 to 4.5 ). Learners on the residuals do so on the unseen class, after retraining on intervention labels (Table ) and with 10% of the fields hidden, the MLP trained with masks on test and the residual MLP on unseen families; late fusions do so on satellite pairs after learning from labeled pairs, as does Qwen3-VL-32B on photographs of unseen families. With the axiom’s 8 seeds, the auxiliary loss points higher on test pseudo-masks (Section 4.6 , Appendix ).

section: Robustness to the label oracle and the visibility threshold.
content: Two further oracles exclude test and out-of-distribution aircraft: the first is fitted on the 44 training aircraft with the paper’s tolerances, the second on the 61 training and validation aircraft with tolerances chosen by leaving one family out. On intervention labels, under both oracles, NeSySpec keeps its leads over Fellegi-Holt and Z3 in diagnosis and over minimum-cardinality localization with random tie-break on every split. It keeps its macro-F1 lead over the DL2-loss network on unseen families under both oracles, on test under the first and slightly under the second, and on the unseen class under the first only. Its narrower leads over the oracle tie-break, the crisp edits and the Class I residual become on par or lower on some splits. Its own levels on test are lower (macro-F1 0.488 and 0.537, abduction 0.532 and 0.491, key 0.732 and, slightly, 0.738, against 0.575, 0.593 and 0.786), and its false violations rise only under the paper’s tolerances, whose bands flag 38 of the 63 clean held-out aircraft and narrow the bands it learns (Appendix ). Re-selected on validation alone, the part detector’s visibility threshold becomes 0.25. Retrained at 0.25, the photograph module keeps its comparisons against the networks without a localization term or with permuted masks and against RRR, GradMask and Pukdee et al. on PASCAL-Part, all kept at 0.20, against the auxiliary loss also retrained at 0.25 and against the vision-language models. Its pointing is slightly lower on test pseudo-masks (0.774 against 0.780) and on PASCAL-Part human masks (0.711 against 0.737), where the auxiliary loss falls as well (0.708 against 0.739), and its cross-modal AUROC is slightly lower on unseen families and the unseen class (Appendix ).

title: NeSySpec: Neuro-Symbolic Technical Intelligence for Auditing Engineering Specifications with an Application to Aircraft
authors: Pier Mattia Basciano, Gianvito Antenori, Cristiano Andolfi, Giovanni Farina, Salvatore Monteleone
content: For every available constraint of a record, NeSySpec returns a graded degree and, by the fixed rule of Section 3.7 , a held or violated constraint verdict (Figures 4 and 5 ); these verdicts reach a macro-F1 of 0.795 on generator-label test and, without retraining, 0.575 on intervention-label test. Against a network trained with the DL2 loss on the same residuals and per-constraint targets, which returns a probability per constraint, they reach a higher macro-F1 on every split and both label families (the network at 0.661 and 0.426 on the two tests; Figure 6 a), and the same key read from the network ranks the violated constraint first less often on every generator-label split (0.752 against 0.942). They also find every labeled violation of a corrupted record more often than the network on every split and both label families (0.934 against 0.522 on generator-label test; micro recall 0.959 against 0.635), with micro precision on par on test and lower on the unseen class (0.458 against 0.577 on generator and 0.517 against 0.639 on intervention labels; Appendix ). With the network’s thresholds tuned on validation the macro-F1 lead holds on generator-label test and is slight on intervention-label test (0.575 against 0.541; Table ). The network reports fewer false violations on clean records (0.020 against 0.074 on generator-label test, also on intervention labels), and NeSySpec also returns the altered field and a repair proposal from the same degrees.

content: On clean and control test records the constraint verdicts report a violation in 0.074 of the checks (Figure 4 ), mostly on A2 and A5 (0.255 and 0.208 of their checks), where A2 evaluates the cruise lift coefficient at maximum take-off mass and A5 uses class-level latents; the report shows which relation the declared values strain and by how far (Figure 5 c), and the key and abduction rank the degrees without this rule.

title: NeSySpec: Neuro-Symbolic Technical Intelligence for Auditing Engineering Specifications with an Application to Aircraft
authors: Pier Mattia Basciano, Gianvito Antenori, Cristiano Andolfi, Giovanni Farina, Salvatore Monteleone
content: The largest degree, the largest-violation key, names the violated constraint in 0.942 of corrupted test records (generator labels; on each of 8 seeds), above Fellegi-Holt, Z3 and rule diagnosis (0.795 to 0.857; Figure 6 b); 49 to 85% of these margins come from the 16 test records that the crisp edits leave unflagged (key 0.812, chance 0.106), and on the 140 they flag it is on par with them. On the 81 test records with a single violated constraint the key reaches 0.963, above the class-standardized residual, a z-score of the same residuals, and MLP-SHAP, which are on par with it over all corrupted test records; it comes with a held or violated verdict against learned tolerances, the altered field with its repair and exact abstention under missing evidence, all read from NeSySpec’s own degrees, and the residual’s field ranking is below abduction (Section 4.3 ). On unseen families the key reaches 0.973 on each of 8 seeds, above Fellegi-Holt, Z3, MLP-SHAP and LightGBM-SHAP and on par with the class-standardized residual, with the rules at 0.863 (cells without an alternative-stream check; Appendix ), and on the unseen class 0.897 ± 0.007 0.897\pm 0.007 , above Fellegi-Holt, Z3, the rules and the class-standardized residual and on par with LightGBM-SHAP, with MLP-SHAP, a second model on the residuals, at 0.970 (Table ). On intervention labels without retraining, the key ranks first a constraint whose scope contains the altered field in 0.786 ± 0.006 0.786\pm 0.006 of corrupted test records (chance 0.232), above Fellegi-Holt, Z3 and rule diagnosis, with most of these margins from the 76 records that the crisp edits leave unflagged, and on par with LightGBM-SHAP, the strongest attribution on these labels; on unseen families NeSySpec’s second head, its secondary key, reaches 0.848 (largest-violation key 0.828; Appendix ). With the optional rank-then-explain setting, NeSySpec flags and correctly diagnoses 0.901 ± 0.013 0.901\pm 0.013 of corrupted test records and 0.849 ± 0.043 0.849\pm 0.043 on the unseen class (5 seed pairs), above Fellegi-Holt and Z3 behind the same alarm on test and on par with MLP-SHAP, with the violated constraint, the altered field and a repair from its own degrees; with its own alarm, the record verdict and the key reach 0.929 on test (Appendix ).

content: Figure 5 shows the report of the first single-field corruption of the test split whose altered field an available constraint reads, chosen by a fixed rule. Its total thrust is altered: the report names A4, the thrust-to-weight ratio below the band learned from the fleet, as the largest violation, abduction finds the thrust, and changing the thrust alone brings V V below the decision threshold (0.181 against 0.310). A9, flagged by the oracle’s crisp band, is held, its thrust per engine inside the wider learned band; A5, which does not read the thrust, is violated as on the clean record (asterisk in panel b), so the repair, short of its stricter target, is a best-effort value to cross-check.

title: NeSySpec: Neuro-Symbolic Technical Intelligence for Auditing Engineering Specifications with an Application to Aircraft
authors: Pier Mattia Basciano, Gianvito Antenori, Cristiano Andolfi, Giovanni Farina, Salvatore Monteleone
content: Abduction names the altered field more often than minimum-cardinality localization on every split, on generated and on independently labeled errors, and needs no oracle to break ties (Figure 6 c). On single-field test corruptions (generator labels) it finds the altered field in 0.742 ± 0.011 0.742\pm 0.011 , above minimum-cardinality localization (0.367) and the Ochiai ranking of the class-standardized residuals; with the oracle tie-break, the setting most favorable to it, minimum-cardinality localization reaches 0.629, on par with abduction. On single-field records that no oracle selected or certified, abduction through the verifier fitted on generator labels, without retraining, finds the field moved beyond tolerance in 0.593 of test records, above minimum-cardinality localization (0.306) and its oracle tie-break (0.453); 78% of the margin over the oracle tie-break comes from the 70 records that the crisp edits leave unflagged, and on the 175 of 245 that they flag abduction stays above random tie-breaking and on par with the oracle tie-break. With the selected abduction rule (Appendix ), abduction is also ahead of the Class I sizing-regression residual, the field farthest from the conceptual-design (Class I) weight regressions on maximum take-off mass fitted on the training aircraft [ 71 ] , on test (0.597), on the unseen class (0.119) and on intervention labels (0.453, the level of the oracle tie-break as well), and on par with it on unseen families (0.693), with the violated constraint and a repair from the same verdict.

authors: Pier Mattia Basciano, Gianvito Antenori, Cristiano Andolfi, Giovanni Farina, Salvatore Monteleone
content: The repair proposal of Eq. ( 13 ) comes from NeSySpec’s own abduction and verdict, with the field and the violated constraint in the same report. It cuts the log-space error on the altered field from 0.366 to 0.133 and on the whole record to 0.200, and is closer on the record than the Fellegi-Holt, MaxSMT, nearest-neighbor and regression repairs and on the altered field than a constraint-layer repair ordering in the style of PiShield [ 47 ] ; at the field of the Class I residual, MICE [ 83 ] (0.120 and 0.161) and missForest are on par with it on both errors, as is the regression on the altered field (Table ). The solver reaches its target, a verdict V ≤ − ln ⁡ 0.9 ≈ 0.1054 V\leq-\ln 0.9\approx 0.1054 stricter than the decision threshold, on 0.555 of the single-field test records and otherwise returns its best-effort value (Figure 5 c); the report issues a proposal for each flagged record, as a value to cross-check.

Further comparisons should distinguish prior recognition from reasoning over the supplied physical constraints.

Loss weights are selected on validation using one seed per candidate value (Appendix ). Under this common protocol, the network trained with the grounding axiom localizes the annotated parts substantially better than RRR [ 57 ] and GradMask [ 58 ] . section: 4.8 What the Logic Adds: Other Encodings of the Same Knowledge
content: The logical formulation provides the constraint-level verdicts used for diagnosis and repair. For record-level detection, learners on the same residuals perform similarly to NeSySpec in distribution and better on the unseen class (Section 4.4 ). Against the network trained with the DL2 loss on the same residuals and targets, which learns one head per constraint in place of the graded predicates and is their like-for-like test, NeSySpec’s graded predicates trained through Real Logic give constraint verdicts with a higher macro-F1 and a better key, with the field and a repair from the same degrees (Section 4.2 ). Of the other Real Logic properties of Section 2.1 , guarded quantification gives the exact abstention that none of 207 learned method and cell rows keeps without an image (Section 4.5 ), the shared truth scale the fused verdict (Section 4.4 ) and the gate grounding stable across loss weights (Section 4.6 ). Stratification (E4) keeps one verdict per evidence source, so the report says whether the record or the image raised the flag (Appendix ). Training the knowledge base through the differentiable truths of Real Logic improves detection over keeping it at its initial values: AUROC rises from 0.907 to 0.979 on test and from 0.845 to 0.934 on the unseen class. On generator labels, the full model outperforms the flat-bank ablation on every split. Removing in-band grading lowers detection on the unseen class and slightly on test and unseen families. The ablation using a generalized mean at p = 4 p=4 is on par with the full model (Table ). In detection on test the record verdict (0.979) is slightly above the DL2-loss network (0.965) and a per-constraint monotone model on the same residual magnitudes without LTN (0.966), and on par with the network out of distribution; NeSySpec reads these magnitudes as graded predicates in physical units (Figure 5 c), with the key, abduction and repair from the same degrees. The generator’s per-constraint targets (Section 4.2 ) and the graded predicates act together: the ablation trained with the binary record label only equals the generator labels in 0.081 of test records and is below the crisp edits on all three measures. Given as a constraint loss on the declared fields or as rules in words, the same knowledge detects less than NeSySpec’s verdict: the DL2 method on the declared fields reaches 0.703 ± 0.030 0.703\pm 0.030 and a language model prompted with the constraints A1-A11 in words (Qwen3-8B [ 52 ] , anonymized records) 0.620, below the record verdict on every split (Table ), and both are below its key and verdicts (Section 4.2 ).

content: Each limitation is bounded by the protocol and opens a line of future work (Section 5 ). Domain and use. NeSySpec is validated on aircraft, whose public civil records and relations a reader can verify; only its knowledge base, visual predicates, corruption generator and data are domain-specific (Appendix A ), and its verdicts support a human analyst, with aircraft detection, tracking and identification outside its scope because of the dual-use risks of such capabilities [ 93 ] . Synthetic errors and scale. Every error is generated or edited, so its type, magnitude and field are known and each verdict is checked against them, and the intervention labels are independent of the generator; they mark the constraints an edit involves, about a third of the altered rows break none of them physically, and expert per-constraint physical labels will score the verdicts against violations (Section 5 ); the 107 aircraft and one published split hold every test family and satellite site out of training. Naturally occurring errors, expert red teams, larger fleets and a replication on a new fleet will extend this evidence. Class-level relations. A2 evaluates the cruise lift coefficient at maximum take-off mass and A5 uses latents shared by a class and engine type, estimable from 44 training aircraft; most violations reported on clean records come from these two relations (Section 4.2 ), which per-type latents and a cruise-weight form of A2 will refine. Classes without training aircraft. There, residual learners rank higher in record-level detection (Section 4.4 ); the optional rank-then-explain setting lets such a learner raise the alarm while NeSySpec names the constraint, the field and a repair, and larger fleets will reduce the classes read with fleet statistics alone. Omission. A withheld field masks the axioms that read it, the exact abstention of Proposition 1 ; the optional critical-field alert flags the omission, and class-level axioms will make the omission of a critical field a violation. Masks, statistics and encodings. Automatic pseudo-masks supervise the grounding axiom, so the protocol is reproducible from public data, and hand-annotated part masks will extend it; no multiplicity correction is applied, which the new-fleet replication will address; encoding the knowledge base in DeepProbLog, Scallop or PSL, with probabilistic facts and proofs, changes its axiomatic and logical structure and is left to a dedicated comparison.

title: NeSySpec: Neuro-Symbolic Technical Intelligence for Auditing Engineering Specifications with an Application to Aircraft
authors: Pier Mattia Basciano, Gianvito Antenori, Cristiano Andolfi, Giovanni Farina, Salvatore Monteleone
content: NeSySpec is an integrated and interpretable neuro-symbolic framework for auditing engineering specifications: its graded axioms on Logic Tensor Networks, trained on fleet data, determine which physical constraints a declared specification respects and which it violates, and from the degree behind each verdict it derives the altered field, a repair proposal, exact abstention on missing evidence, part-grounded image evidence and a verification report. Validated on 107 aircraft with generated, intervention-labeled and falsified errors, it provides and evaluates these outputs together.

Minimum-cardinality localization reaches 0.306 with random tie-breaking and 0.453 with oracle tie-breaking. The Class I sizing-regression residual also reaches 0.453. title: NeSySpec: Neuro-Symbolic Technical Intelligence for Auditing Engineering Specifications with an Application to Aircraft
authors: Pier Mattia Basciano, Gianvito Antenori, Cristiano Andolfi, Giovanni Farina, Salvatore Monteleone
content: Among the approaches evaluated here (the DL2 method on the declared fields, the network trained with the DL2 loss on the same residuals read per constraint, a constraint-layer repair ordering, LTN ablations, solver and rule diagnosis and prompted language and vision-language models), NeSySpec is, to our knowledge, the most suitable neuro-symbolic framework for auditing engineering specifications: it provides and evaluates together the outputs of Table 2 , and its key and abduction lead classical diagnosis, the DL2 method, a prompted language model and minimum-cardinality localization with random tie-breaking. No comparator returns all the outputs of the audit, and on the test aircraft none is ahead of NeSySpec in the macro-F1 of the constraint verdicts, in naming the violated constraint and the altered field or in the repair error on the altered field (Table 5 ). With oracles fitted without test or out-of-distribution aircraft, its leads on intervention labels over Fellegi-Holt and Z3 in diagnosis and over minimum-cardinality localization with random tie-breaking hold on every split, at lower levels (Section 4.1 ). Its logic serves the physical audit more than record classification: in record-level detection, learners on the same residuals are close to it and in some settings rank records higher (Section 4.4 ). Its detection grows with the knowledge it encodes, following the share of edits that alter a field its constraints read, with diminishing returns in their number.

section: B.1 Example of a Verification Report
content: Figure (Section ) shows a report assembled from the saved outputs of NeSySpec (train prior, seed 0) for a record chosen by a rule fixed before any value was read: the first single-field corruption of the test split, in file order, whose altered field an available constraint reads. The corruption divides the total thrust of a narrow-body turbofan by 1.2, and the generator oracle flags A4 and A9. The verdict flags the record ( V = 1.217 V=1.217 , above the validation threshold t ⋆ = 0.310 t^{\star}=0.310 of this seed), and the report lists the degree of every available constraint, the largest being A4 (10.001), A5 (1.053), A8 (0.386) and A9 (0.384). By the rule of Section , A4 and A5 exceed ln ⁡ 2 \ln 2 and are violated, A5 also on the clean record, while A8 and A9 are held.
